about.title: Brisbane Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Brisbane is small — a San Mateo County city of about 4,700 people — and when a fatal collision happens here, it is felt across the whole town. Public records for 2025 list one traffic death within city limits, alongside 27 injury collisions that left 35 people hurt. The corridors that appear most often in those records are US-101, Bayshore Boulevard, the US-101 northbound lanes and Guadalupe Canyon Parkway, with reports clustering on Thursday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. Behind that single fatality is a family in San Mateo County now facing a funeral, lost income and an empty chair. California law gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, generally within two years of the death, and sooner if a public agency may be at fault. LawProactive exists to take one task off your plate: we connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you can focus on your family.

whyChoose.title: Why Brisbane Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can tell you plainly where your family stands.

items.title: The two-year clock, explained
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early guidance helps protect that deadline.

items.title: Every loss accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to the financial support your loved one provided and the love, companionship and guidance your family has lost. This is a civil action, separate from any criminal case.

items.question: My spouse was killed on US-101 through Brisbane. Does it matter if Caltrans or the city is involved?
items.answer: It can matter a great deal. When a government entity may share fault — for example over a roadway condition on US-101 or Guadalupe Canyon Parkway — California requires a formal claim to be filed with that agency well before the usual two-year deadline. An attorney can determine quickly whether that shorter timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from any criminal prosecution in San Mateo County. Your family can pursue compensation whether or not the driver is convicted, and the two-year deadline continues to run regardless of the criminal case.

items.question: What does it cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means no fee unless there is a recovery for your family.
